DIRECTORS’ REPORT
Financial Performance

OP
Y

In its third year of operation, the Company focused on building a strong foundation while
navigating a challenging external environment marked by economic uncertainty and high
inflation. The Company laid the groundwork for future growth and sustainability. The focus
remained on strengthening operational frameworks and positioning the Company for long-term
success.

Economy

EC

During the year, Pakistan’s operating environment remained under pressure, with high inflation
and a depreciating currency eroding consumer purchasing power. In addition, political
uncertainty and frequent policy changes continued to create challenges for businesses.

TR
U

Amid these headwinds, certain sectors such as technology and agriculture exhibited growth
prospects, while the retail industry sustained its positive momentum. This growth was driven by a
rising middle class, rapid urbanization, and the continued shift towards e-commerce, particularly
in the post-pandemic era.

Real Estate / REIT Sector

IFI
ED

At the same time, competition within the retail sector intensified as both local and international
brands expanded their market presence. Nevertheless, the adoption of innovative retail solutions,
coupled with a focus on enhanced customer experiences, has enabled retailers to adapt
successfully and remain resilient in a dynamic business environment

CE
RT

The real estate sector in Pakistan is navigating a transformative phase amid economic
adjustments and regulatory reforms. Despite challenges like fluctuating macroeconomic
conditions and policy shifts, the industry shows resilience with sustained interest in residential and
commercial properties. Urbanization remains a key driver, fueling demand for housing and
infrastructure projects in major cities. Moreover, advancements in technology and sustainability
are shaping new trends, influencing development practices and consumer expectations.
Government initiatives to promote housing affordability and infrastructure development are
expected to further boost market confidence. Looking ahead, the industry is confident for
strategic growth, driven by innovative approaches, digital integration, and proactive adaptation
to evolving market dynamics and consumer preferences.
Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) are emerging as a significant force in Pakistan’s real estate
market, offering investors a streamlined path to passive income and portfolio diversification. Their
ability to attract both institutional and retail investors positions them as a key element of the
investment landscape. Supportive regulatory reforms by the SECP have lowered entry barriers and
spurred unprecedented investment in the REIT sector.
The future of REITs in Pakistan looks bright, driven by increasing investor interest, regulatory backing,
and evolving market dynamics. Continued innovation, investor education, and regulatory
improvements are expected to further accelerate the growth of REITs, contributing significantly to
the development of Pakistan’s property market.

Governance
The Company adopts a forward-thinking approach to corporate governance, ensuring full
adherence to the Listed Companies (Corporate Governance) Regulations, 2019 (CCG). Our
compliance statement, which has been reviewed and approved by external auditors, is featured
in this annual report, reflecting our dedication to maintaining the highest levels of governance
and transparency.

Y

Board of Directors

EC

The Company prides itself on having a strong and diverse Board of Directors, consisting of
individuals with a wide array of skills, expertise, and experience. This diversity ensures a wealth of
perspectives and knowledge, enabling the Board to effectively steer the Company’s strategic
direction. As on 30 June 2025, the Board includes seven (7) members, with four (4) Non-Executive
Directors (NEDs) representing shareholders and two (2) Independent Directors (IDs). Current

Annual Evaluation of the performance of the Board, Board’s Committees and
Individual Directors
As the Company is currently in its formation stage and has not yet commenced operations, a
formal mechanism for annual performance evaluation is in developmental stage. However, the
Company plans to ensure full compliance with applicable laws and regulations once company
becomes fully operational.

CE
RT

Compensation for Directors

Pursuant to the Directors’ Service Agreement, Independent Directors are paid a fee for attending
Board meetings. The CEO, who is the only executive director on the Board, along with nonindependent directors, the Company Secretary, and the CFO, are employees of the Zameen
Group. As such, they do not receive any remuneration from the Company. Additionally, the CEO
is not paid any extra fees for attending Board meetings.

Directors’ Compliance Statement
The Board affirms the following:

OP
Y

- Proper books of accounts have been maintained.
- The financial statements prepared by management accurately and fairly reflect the Company’s
financial position, operational results, cash flows, and changes in equity.
- There is no significant uncertainty regarding the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern.
- Appropriate accounting policies, consistent with International Financial Reporting Standards (as
applicable in Pakistan), have been applied in the preparation of the financial statements. Accounting
estimates, where necessary, are based on reasonable and prudent judgment.
- There have been no material deviations from the best practices of corporate governance.

Audit and Risk Oversight Committee

In compliance with the Code of Corporate Governance, the Audit and Risk Oversight Committee has
continued to operate in accordance with its Terms of Reference, which have been formally approved
by the Board.

EC

Internal Audit

TR
U

The Internal Audit function of the Company has been established and will operate following
commencement of formal REIT operations. The Board highly values the insights and recommendations
provided by the Audit and Risk Oversight Committee regarding the adequacy and effectiveness of the
Company’s internal controls and ensures timely and appropriate actions are taken.

Ethics & Compliance

In compliance with the Listed Companies (Code of Corporate Governance) Regulations, 2019, the
'Code of Conduct' has been shared with all Directors of the Company.

Appointment of Auditors

IFI
ED

EY Ford Rhodes & Co. Chartered Accountants, the auditors of the Company for FY 2024-25, are retiring
and have offered themselves for reappointment.
The external auditors have received a satisfactory rating under the Quality Control Review Program of
the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan (ICAP). They have confirmed compliance with the
Listed Companies (Corporate Governance) Regulations 2019 and the International Federation of
Accountants (IFAC) guidelines on the Code of Ethics, as adopted by ICAP.

CE
RT

Additionally, the external auditors have not been engaged to provide any other services that could
impair their independence, and they have confirmed adherence to IFAC guidelines in this regard.

Related Party Transactions

OP
Y

In adherence to the REIT Regulations and the Code of Corporate Governance, the Company
submitted all related party transactions to the Audit and Risk Oversight Committee and the Board of
the Company for review and approval. These transactions were subsequently approved by both the
Audit and Risk Oversight Committee and the Board of Directors during their respective meetings. Further
details of these related party transactions are outlined in Note 14 of the accompanying audited
financial statements.

of the Management and employees, whose efforts have been pivotal to the Company’s success.
